issues.body: The new sentence in `starvation_provenance_escalation_body` — "The scheduled provenance sweep records it within one cadence." — is unconditional, but `backfill-provenance.yml`'s own header documents that a PR it cannot resolve (log unreadable / no anchored source / sources disagree / partial evidence / binding mismatch / author mismatch) is reported and left fail-closed invisible. Run-log retention and GitHub's scheduled-workflow behaviour are further reasons a sweep may not clear a given holder. An operator reading this receipt may wait out a cadence for a record that will never land, which is the same "hold whose exit nobody can find" failure mode (#703) the receipt exists to prevent — just relocated from "no remedy named" to "remedy named that may not fire". The census one-liner at :2747 carries the same unconditional phrasing ("records these within one cadence").
issues.fix_hint: Soften to something like "The scheduled provenance sweep attempts this every cadence; it leaves the PR recordless with a named reason when the run log cannot bind an implementer identity." Same qualifier in `format_unprovenanced_narrowed_census`.
issues.title: Receipt promises unconditional auto-recovery, but backfill can legitimately fail to resolve a PR

issues.body: The census string is pinned exactly (two tripwires), but the receipt's new claim is only reachable through the substring asserts at :23383-23392, none of which mention the scheduled sweep. Per this file's own doctrine at :23390 ("Unasserted, this qualifier could be reverted green"), the sentence that tells an operator recovery is automatic can be deleted without reding any self-test — the same gap that let the now-corrected "nothing triggers it" wording persist after #1544 landed.
issues.fix_hint: Add one assert next to the existing receipt asserts, e.g. `assert "scheduled provenance sweep" in receipt, receipt`, matching the phrasing chosen for the first issue.
issues.title: New scheduled-sweep sentence in the escalation receipt is unasserted and could be reverted green

verdict.summary:
Message/comment-only change to scripts/dispatch-claim.py: the unprovenanced-narrowed census line, the starvation_provenance_escalation docstring, and the operator receipt in starvation_provenance_escalation_body are updated to stop asserting that backfill-provenance is workflow_dispatch-only with no automatic recovery. VERIFIED against the checkout at PR head: .github/workflows/backfill-provenance.yml now carries `schedule: cron '23 */4 * * *'` (added under #1544), the targets job resolves EVERY enabled policy row when no target_repo is supplied (which is what a schedule supplies), and APPLY is `${{ inputs.apply || github.event_name == 'schedule' }}`, so a scheduled run really does write records across all enabled targets on a four-hour cadence. The new prose therefore matches reality and the old prose no longer did.

No behaviour change: no control flow, routing precedence, reservation/lease logic, gate, permission, or classifier is touched. Nothing is weakened — the escalation still fires, still does not free the partition, still names the manual backfill and the area-label partial recovery, and the fail-closed reservation is untouched.

Test validity: the two exact-string tripwires at scripts/dispatch-claim.py:19111 and :19284 are updated in lockstep with the emitter at :2747 and I diffed them character-for-character — they still pin the whole stdout of that leg, so dropping or conditioning the census emission still reds them. Non-vacuous. The receipt self-test at :23382 asserts substrings that all survive the rewording (`backfill-provenance`, `apply=true`, the `declares no area:* label` qualifier, the labelling clause), so it stays green legitimately rather than by accident. No stale copy of the old wording remains anywhere in the tree (grepped).

Two minor accuracy/coverage notes below; neither blocks. No token/PII surface, no workflow expansion of untrusted text, nothing to arm.
